content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. A single creature combining a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. The head is that of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur on the face and a plain coat with no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body, a head horn grown from the frontal bone of the head, above and between the eyes, out of the covering, which continues from there into the body covering of smooth, glossy dark cuticle, with one horn curving upward and back from the head; hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, grown from the skin as the brown bear's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, shoulders, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs, and tail, replacing the brown bear's dense fur there and conforming to the brown bear's body, each plate sized to the brown bear's own body segments and muscle masses, one plate per segment or muscle mass, joined by flexible cuticle at every joint; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face retains the brown bear's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape and bends at every joint. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws, and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

I'm planning a natural history illustration that merges a brown bear's body and head with a rhinoceros beetle's glossy chitin plates and a single frontal horn, in a full-body side three-quarter view on a plain light background.
**Crafting hybrid bear illustration**
I'm preparing a natural history illustration of a single brown bear with chitin plates, a rhinoceros beetle-style horn, and visible spiracles, shown in a side three-quarter view on a plain light background.
**Refining hybrid bear design**
I'm preparing another generation to blend the armor plates more seamlessly with natural fur, especially around the face, while keeping the spiracles and overall look.
